description: Prompt, retrieval, examples and tools, fine-tuning, training: options from cheapest to most expensive. Climb only when evals show the lower rung fails.
Changing what the model sees (prompt, retrieved documents, examples, tools). Versioned like code, instant to roll back, survives a model swap.
Changing the model itself (fine-tuning, preference tuning, training). Creates a new artifact that needs data, compute, hosting and retraining when the base moves.
Training a pretrained model further on input-output examples of the behavior you want.
Training a model further on a large unlabeled corpus (a domain or a language) before any task tuning. Rarely needed by product teams.
Fine-tuning teaches behavior (format, style, narrow skills) well and knowledge poorly; changing facts belong in retrieval.
